Aquino St. Fort San Pedro loilo City Dear RD Ingeniero: This refers to your Memorandum seeking guidance on the Regional Office's authority to enter into a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the Barangay Councilor's League of the Philippines (BCLP) as one of its partners under the Local Governance Resource Center (LGRC). As you stated, the MOA seeks to establish a partnership between DILG Regional Office VI and BCLP in carrying out programs particularly in the areas of: (1) capacity development of the BCLP and its members, (2) anti-drug abuse campaign, (3) environmental management, and (4) disaster preparedness. We discuss. Functions of a Regional Office We find the need to discuss first the functions of a Regional Office as an integral part of the administrative structure of our government. Pursuant to Section 26 of Executive Order 292, s. 19871, a Regional Office, within its administrative region, is given the task to implement laws, policies, rules and regulations as well as plans and programs of the department or agency. . — (I) A regional office SECTION 26. Functions of a Regional Office shall: a. Implement laws, policies, plans, programs, rules and regulations of the department or agency in the regional area; YYY Local Govemance Resource Center The general guidelines for the establishment of Local Governance Resource Centers is governed by DILG Memorandum Circular 2022-052 issued on 29 April 2022 and entitled "Operationalizing Knowledge Management in Local Governance Resource Administrative Code cf 1987 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline Noa 8876-34-54

Centers". In it, LGRC is defined as a dynamic and interactive convergence platform that contributes to buildin DILG as a Knowled e Centric Or anization and builds learning communities that pursues local governance excellence through knowledge sharin and innovation. The LGRC serves a delive mechanism of the DILG in implementing programs aligned to its outcome framework. DILG MC 2022-052 stipulates that the maintenance of LGRC rest on the principle of "multi-stakeholdership participation" which prescribes for the formation of partnership engagements with other national government agencies, CSOs, non-government organizations (NGOs), civil society organization (CSOs), people's organizations (POs), the academe and other stakeholder for collaborative governance initiative. The subject Department issuance also directs that every DILG Regional Office shall have a regional level-LGRC-referred to as Local Governance Regional Resource Centers (LGRRCs) - under the strategic direction of their respective Regional Director. Among other functions, the regional level-LGRC is responsible for organizing "partnerships between and among local governance stakeholders at the regional level" Baranqay Councilor's League of the Philippines (BCLP) The organization of the BCLP is sanctioned under Section 508 of the Local Government Code of 1991 , it states: "Section 508. Organization (a) Vice governors, vice mayors, sanggunian members of barangays, component cities, highly-urbanized cities and provinces, and other elective officials of local government units, including those of Metropolitan Manila area and any metropolitan political subdivisions, may form their respective leagues or federations, subject to applicable provisions of this Title and pertinent provisions of this Code. It is perhaps on account of BCLP's being an aggrupation of elected Sangguniang Barangay Members with which the request for guidance from the concerned Regional Office had sprung. Considering the mandate of the concerned RO under above law and issuance, we find no legal prohibition on the forging of a memorandum of agreement with the BCLP, it appearing that the proposed undertaking is within the authority of the RO as an implementing arm of the Department. Be that as it may, we ought to remind you that, as gathered by the National Barangay Operations Office (NBOO), there were about four (4) organizations or leagues representing as the legitimate organization of sangguniang barangay members in the country-the BLCP, Pederasyon ng mga Barangay Kagawad sa Pilipinas (PBKP), Liga ng mga Barangay Kagawad and I other organization. The foregoing considered, it should be emphasized that the proposed partnership should not be construed as conferring recognition to the BCLP as the only legitimate organization of the duly elected sangguniang barangay members in the country.
